title: Design System: The Atmospheric Builders' Retreat

display.purpose: The stacked retreat name on the hero; line 1 at clamp(3.4rem, 13.5vw, 6rem), line 2 at clamp(2.55rem, 10vw, 4.5rem). Always uppercase, line-height 0.92. The organizer rail title reuses the atom at a one-off rail scale.

headline.purpose: Question titles ('ARE YOU IN?') and the review title.

title.purpose: Denser interactive items: dates calendar and location ranking. Reused verbatim by the organizer's sign-in gate title (a mini hero).

stat.purpose: The organizer rail's display numerals: the title ramp's endpoints (2.2rem–3.6rem) interpolated on viewport HEIGHT (3.2vh) so the full stat stack fits the first viewport. Tabular numerals, min-width 1.6ch.

place.purpose: Location names on the survey; reused verbatim by the organizer's section titles ('When can they come', 'Responses', 'Allowlist').

body.purpose: Prompts and explanatory copy, 38-46ch measure. The hero acknowledgment scales up to clamp(1rem, 1.6vw + 0.7rem, 1.375rem).

label.purpose: Uppercase field labels, rail section heads, table headers, window rank labels, and the status chip (0.6875rem, 0.18em tracking). KEPT by explicit user decision 2026-08-04 as a documented exception to the craft-floor kicker ban; on /organizer it is labels and section heads only, never an eyebrow — the survey hero's kicker is the sole eyebrow use. Ledger facts use the sibling 0.8125rem / 0.14em style.

reading.purpose: Organizer-written prose on the home (44ch; 48ch under lead photos, 60ch in posts).

caption.purpose: Figure captions, nav times and current light, clock tags.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing in the world; every transition and the settle use it.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The one authored motion, feed-only (survey items, registration flow): item content settles upward when it enters (IntersectionObserver threshold 0.4). Gated on html.js; neutralized under prefers-reduced-motion. The home and the organizer have zero entrances.

motion.name: chrome
motion.purpose: Rail stops, progress dots, and the organizer's tally-bar scale.

motion.name: state-micro
motion.purpose: Calendar cells, chips, option rows, switch knob, filter segments, table-row expanders.

motion.name: nav-yield
motion.purpose: The home gutter nav fades out while a lead photograph passes beneath it; keyboard focus brings it back.

motion.name: smooth-anchor
motion.purpose: In-page jumps from the time-of-day nav on the home.

narrative.overview:
Every surface is the Southern California dusk — photographed, or the near-black ground the photographs settle into — and the interface is a single voice speaking over it in pure white. The feed (the original survey, and now the registration flow at `/?register`) refuses the centered-card stepper on a gray ground: it is a feed you flick through, one item per viewport, snap-scrolled like the social product its audience lives in. The photography — real Wikimedia location shots and labeled synthetic desert-modern atmosphere — carries all of the color; the UI contributes exactly one ink.

Density is low and bottom-weighted. Each item breathes at the top (a flex spacer, `min-height: 8–12vh`) and settles its content toward the bottom edge, where a scrim gradient darkens the photograph to near-black so text never negotiates with the image. Structure is drawn, not boxed: hairline rules at 35% white separate ledger rows; the only filled container in the world is the fully-rounded white pill. A film-grain tile at 7% overlay unifies photographic sources into one material.

The world now has a second surface: the organizer room (`/organizer`) is the same night at **Operate density**. The photographs stay home — the ground is the solid dusk near-black carrying the same grain at its flat-surface blend — and the one ink does data work: a command rail of condensed display numerals on the left, an availability heatmap whose cells are computed white alpha, hairline ledgers and tables in the content column. It refuses the KPI-card dashboard-on-gray the way the survey refuses the stepper. Density rises; the material does not change.

The world's third surface is the retreat home at `/`: **one long evening**. It no longer snaps a feed; it scrolls freely through stacked regions of light that deepen as you go — golden hour (the hero, then organizer-written story and plan sections over a blurred, inverted copy of the hero's own light), blue hour (Who's coming, over a dusk photograph), and night (the posts stream on the solid ground). Regions overlap and fade into one another through masked photographs and ground-colored scrims, so the light changes with no seam. Each region opens on an **evening-clock line** — a ruled ledger row reading a time and a light ("4:52 PM · Blue hour") — and a slim time-of-day nav tracks where you are in the evening. Sections that carry photographs become regions of their own: the lead photo full-bleed at the hero's strength, the copy settling onto its scrimmed lower edge. Everything else the home lists — schedules, packing lists, people, posts — is a hairline ledger.

The world was chosen deliberately over the assigned direction (user-chosen challenger, seed `9380440b`) and its finish bar is written into the layout contract: unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished.
keyCharacteristics: One UI color: white, stepped only by opacity (100 / 70 / 45 / 35 / 12 — plus 14 and 7 as data-density steps).
Full-bleed photographic grounds under ground-colored scrims on the feed and the home's light regions; solid `#0b0908` ground at night and on operate surfaces; the grain tile everywhere.
Ultra-condensed stacked display caps (Big Shoulders) against a quiet grotesk body (Hanken Grotesk).
Hairline ledger rows for facts, options, and data; the white pill as the single filled action.
Three cadences, one world: the feed snap-scrolls one item per viewport; the home scrolls freely through regions of deepening light; the organizer scrolls freely under a sticky command rail.
Evening-clock lines open every home region; time of day is the home's navigation.
One authored motion: content settles upward 28px when a feed item snaps in. The home and the organizer have zero entrances.
1.75-stroke outline icon system; the filled Bluesky butterfly is the lone deliberate outsider.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: The interface owns exactly one color: white. Hierarchy is opacity (70/45/35/14/12/7), never a second hue. If a design needs another color, it comes from a photograph.

rules.name: The Computed Ink Rule
rules.body: When ink encodes data (the availability heatmap), intensity is white alpha computed from the data — `0.05 + 0.95 × (count / peak)`, floored so a single person stays visible against zero — and the cell numeral flips from ink to ground when the cell's mean alpha exceeds 0.5, so contrast is computed, not blended. Data never gets a color scale; it gets more or less of the one ink.

rules.name: The Scrim Guarantee Rule
rules.body: Text never sits on raw photography. Every feed item carries a bottom-weighted gradient from transparent to 90–98% `#0b0908` (a `darker` variant exists for dense items like the calendar); location cards carry a left-to-right equivalent. On the home, the hero clears through its middle and closes at 0.97 ground; a lead photo's scrim clears through its upper half and reaches the solid ground at the photo's foot, where the copy sits; the golden region holds 0.97 → 0.62 over its blurred light (0.9 at the foot when it runs straight into night); blue hour runs 0.62 → solid ground. Contrast is guaranteed by the scrim, not negotiated per photo. The flat ground needs no scrim; the guarantee there is the ground itself.

rules.name: The Ground-Stop Rule
rules.body: Every scrim is the Dusk Ground at stepped alpha (`rgb(11 9 8 / a)`), never `#000` or a tinted overlay, and the stop where one region ends meets the stop where the next begins (the hero's last 0.97 is golden's first). The night is the same ground at full strength; the light going out is the ground's alpha rising.

rules.name: The Stacked Caps Rule
rules.body: Display type is always uppercase, always `line-height: 0.92`, and multi-line titles stack as separate spans that may differ in size. Never letter-space display caps beyond 0.005em.

rules.name: The Kicker Exception
rules.body: The uppercase kicker/eyebrow (`.kicker`) is normally banned by the craft floor, but it is KEPT in this world by explicit user decision (2026-08-04), which overrides the ban. It is a documented exception scoped to this project: use the `.kicker` atom exactly as defined; do not invent additional eyebrow variants. On the organizer surfaces (`/organizer`, `/organizer/retreat`, `/organizer/retreat/attendees`) the kicker appears only as field labels, list/group heads ("Sections", "On the site", "Not shown"), and stat labels — never as an eyebrow above a heading. The one sanctioned eyebrow is the hero's retreat kicker, which moved with the hero from the survey to the home at `/`; no other surface gets one.

rules.name: The Clock Is a Ledger Rule
rules.body: The evening-clock line that opens a home region is a ledger row, not an eyebrow: hairline top and bottom, Fact metrics, time in tabular Ink, light in Ink 70. Its words come only from the evening table in content (time + light, plus the "Invited only" tag on invited lead sections) — never an invented label, and never on a surface that is not the home's evening.

rules.name: The One Viewport Rule
rules.body: One feed item owns the entire viewport. Nothing scrolls inside an item on the feed axis; if content grows, it earns density (the `darker` scrim), never a second screen. This rule is scoped to the feed — the registration flow at `/?register` and the survey feed items — which `/` itself no longer renders. The home and the organizer scroll freely.

rules.name: The Pairs Not Orphans Rule
rules.body: On the home, short sections pair two-up; an odd last one takes the whole row and splits title-left / body-right, and the console's stat ledger closes square the same way. Nothing sits alone in half a row.

rules.name: The Seamless Evening Rule
rules.body: Home regions never meet at a hard edge: each light runs under the next, photographs fade through masks, and scrim stops meet at matching alphas. Night is reached by the ground's alpha rising, never by a cut.

rules.name: The Flat World Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows, ever. Layering is expressed with scrims, hairlines, backdrop blur, and opacity — never with a shadow vocabulary.

rules.name: The Grain Rule
rules.body: Every ground carries the grain tile (`/media/grain.png`, `background-size: 340px`), blended per surface: photographic grounds at `opacity: 0.07; mix-blend-mode: overlay` (home hero, region light layers, lead photos, every figure frame); flat `#0b0908` grounds at `opacity: 0.05; mix-blend-mode: screen` (status strip, mobile nav, night region — masked in over `12rem` — footer, console pages sized to the whole document). Overlay needs photographic midtones beneath it and vanishes on near-black; screen at the lower opacity is the same grain made visible on a solid ground. Never omit the grain, and never use any other opacity/blend pair.

rules.name: The One Container Rule
rules.body: The fully-rounded white pill is the only filled container in the interface. Round controls (chips, filter segments, the switch) may invert to solid ink in their *selected* state — that reads as state, not surface. Text content is never boxed or carded; it sits directly on the ground, structured by hairlines.

rules.name: The One Settle Rule
rules.body: The caption settle is the only authored entrance in the world. New components may transition state (opacity, transform, ≤0.45s, `--ease-out`) but never add a second choreographed entrance. The home and the organizer hold this at zero: nothing on them animates in.

rules.name: The Butterfly Exception
rules.body: The Bluesky butterfly is a filled brand mark, deliberately outside the 1.75-stroke system — it is a wordmark, not an icon. No other filled glyph is permitted.

dos: **Do** put every surface on the dusk ground — full-bleed photography with the scrim on the feed and the home's light regions, solid `#0b0908` on the night region and operate surfaces — always with the grain tile at its surface's blend (0.07 overlay on photographs, 0.05 screen on flat ground).
**Do** open every home region with an evening-clock line from the content's evening table, and let regions overlap and fade so the light changes without a seam.
**Do** render organizer-written lists as ledgers (`**Label** — value` pairs, `Label — aside` items) and render third-party posts natively in the one ink.
**Do** express all hierarchy as white opacity steps: 1 / 0.7 / 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.12, plus the two data-density steps (0.14 row separators, 0.07 cell keylines) on dense data surfaces — no other alphas.

**Do** set display type in Big Shoulders, 700 (650 for the place/section ramp), uppercase, `line-height: 0.92`, sized with the established clamps — including the height-interpolated Stat ramp for rail numerals.

**Do** structure data as hairline ledgers and tables (`1px solid var(--ink-35)`, 0.14 inside dense tables) and reserve the solid white pill for the single primary action per item or section; secondary actions are the 1.5px outline pill or a quiet link.
**Do** honor `prefers-reduced-motion`, `env(safe-area-inset-*)`, and the `html.js` gate on anything that starts hidden.
donts: **Don't** introduce a second UI color, a gray ramp, or tinted surfaces — even data visualization is computed white alpha, never a color scale.
**Don't** use box-shadows, filled cards, or bordered boxes around text; the pill is the only filled container, KPI cards are refused on the organizer, and Bluesky posts are never embedded or carded.
**Don't** let the home's nav labels sit over a photograph; it yields while a lead photo passes.
**Don't** add icons outside the 1.75-stroke/round-join/24-grid system, and don't fill any glyph except the Bluesky butterfly.
**Don't** author new entrance animations; the snap-in settle is the world's one moment, and the organizer proves screens work with none.

**Don't** let text sit on unscrimmed photography, shrink the gutter/rail clearance (`--gutter` + 2.4rem right on the feed; `11.5rem + --space-5` beside the home's gutter nav), or use the kicker as an eyebrow anywhere except the hero.
